paper.title: Sequential Estimation under Multiple Resources: a Bandit Point of View

unmapped: Arms are d-dimensional Gaussians N(theta, Sigma_i) sharing a common unknown mean theta; the goal is to estimate theta with an unbiased estimator after n rounds

Regret = E||theta_hat - theta||^2 - Tr((n I_{a*})^{-1}), i.e. MSE of the final estimator minus the optimal variance; for Gaussians it equals (1/n^2) sum_i Delta_i E[T_i(n)] with Delta_i = Tr(Sigma_i) - Tr(Sigma*)
Covariance matrices satisfy ||Sigma_i||_F <= Gamma, and the learner knows Gamma
settings.definition_quote: A SEMR problem is a sequential game between a learner and an environment. ... In each round t, the learner first chooses a source A_t and then the environment reveals a sampled data X_t in R^d from that source. ... We restrict our distributions such that P = { N(theta, Sigma) } ... forall i: ||Sigma_i||_F <= Gamma

settings.name_in_paper: SEMR, scalar parameter, general distribution family (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are distributions P_{theta, sigma_i} sharing a common scalar parameter theta, with arm-specific scale sigma_i; the goal is unbiased estimation of theta
Regret = MSE of the final unbiased estimator minus 1/(n I_{a*}) (Fisher information of the best arm)
Reverse-Lipschitz condition on the Fisher information: |I_{sigma_1} - I_{sigma_2}| >= L |sigma_1 - sigma_2|

symbols.Gamma: upper bound on the Frobenius norm of every arm's covariance matrix

conditions: Gaussian arms N(theta, Sigma_i) with common mean
estimator is the sample mean of all observations

source.label: order
source.quote: The LCB algorithm guarantees the following regret bound, Reg(n) \in O(n^{-\frac{3}{2}}\sqrt{\log(n)})

results.notes: Regret is the MSE of the final estimator minus Tr(Sigma*)/n, which equals (1/n^2) sum_i Delta_i E[T_i(n)], so the quantity is 'other'. The proof gives the explicit bound Reg(n) <= 5 sum_i Delta_i/n^2 + 4 Gamma (1+sqrt(max{2,(d-1)^2})) sqrt(2 K log n)/n^{3/2}. It uses Lemma 4, E[T_i(n)] <= C_d log(n)/Delta_i^2 + 5 with C_d = 8 Gamma^2 (1+sqrt(max{2,(d-1)^2}))^2. Lemma 4's statement environment is empty, so it is not recorded separately. The O hides the dependence on K, d and Gamma.

symbols.L: reverse-Lipschitz constant of the Fisher information with respect to sigma

conditions: the final estimator is unbiased (Cramer-Rao is applied)
reverse-Lipschitz Fisher information: |I_{sigma_1} - I_{sigma_2}| >= L|sigma_1 - sigma_2|
hard instances are two environments that differ in one arm

source.label: LowerBound
source.quote: For every policy $\pi$ there is an environment $\nu$ such that $Reg(n) \in \Omega (n^{-\frac{2}{3}})$.

results.notes: The theorem statement prints Omega(n^{-2/3}), but the proof concludes Reg(n) >= C_3 n^{-3/2} with C_3 = L sqrt(k-1)/(4e sqrt(I^{sigma_1}) (I_1^theta)^2). This matches the paper's claim that the bound is order-optimal up to a log factor. The proved n^{-3/2} rate is recorded, and -2/3 is treated as a typo.
